theory.title: Reporting Yesterday in a Stand-up
theory.intro: This lesson reviews past-state language and places it inside a stand-up communication format. The learner starts by saying how yesterday was.
content: A simple stand-up often begins with a short report about yesterday.
Use Yesterday, I was... and We were... to describe past study states.
Use The session was... or The lab was... to evaluate a past event.
The goal is not a long narrative. It is a short, useful retrospective statement.

theory.title: Talking About Tomorrow and the Next Step

theory.title: Building My Daily Stand-up
theory.intro: The final lesson of Week 16 integrates the entire communication cycle of this phase into a daily stand-up style update.
content: A simple stand-up can include three main blocks: yesterday, today and tomorrow.

Today is current status: I am..., I have..., I can join...
Tomorrow points forward: Tomorrow, I have..., My next step is to...
The goal is a short, organized and useful report in a study and tech-oriented environment.
